study.question: Does harmful coupling through the extra semantic-pool gradient paths explain part of the r0040 learned/null validation deficit, even when its forward representation and classifier capacity are retained exactly?
study.hypothesis: Provisional optimization hypothesis, not observed gradient conflict: gradients from the 128 extra pooled-value inputs through shared gate scores and/or shared event values can move representations away from what benefits the complete incumbent path. Stopping these extra paths can recover validation AUC without removing semantic features. r0040 learned/null AUC0.6201982621 is below incumbent0.6209487955, despite a0.0005332515 improvement over learned/mean. In first512, gate saturation0.3610 and zero-extra logit distance0.2402 show substantial branch dependence but cannot establish harmful gradients. All four r0040 cells failed; uniform mean/null also failed, so score gradients alone are not presumed responsible. Short-history and empty-history slices improved while dominant history_gt64 (3026583 samples;151372 positive,2875211 negative) regressed0.6216171077 to0.6209114085. These are exploratory observations, not independent evidence units.

nearest_work.difference: Direct parent and live/live fourth cell. Retain every forward operation and parameter; independently stop only the gate mass/numerator weight path and the explicit numerator value path of the extra branch. Parent relevance and value gradients remain live.

DIN activation and embedding/MLP are inherited prior art. This is a local backward-path intervention on the failed field/action null-pooling extension; not a DIN reproduction or new attention/intensity mechanism.

study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 backward-only factorial: gate gradient live/stop crossed with numerator-value gradient live/stop. Existing r0040-activation_learned_null supplies live/live. Three standalone new modules implement stop/stop, stop/live and live/stop. Gate detach is applied after sigmoid before BOTH numerator weights and normalization mass. Value detach is applied to the numerator operand AFTER the live value has already constructed the gate score; it intentionally leaves the value-to-score path active when gate is live. Stop/stop blocks every extra-pool gradient to the shared representation but leaves all classifier gradients and complete parent paths active. No forward, information, loss, capacity or initialization change. This is an ordinary stop-gradient adaptation with unverified broader nearest work and no novelty priority claim.
predictions: All four routing cells have identical pooled tables and logits at any common parameter state, up to floating-point roundoff; route flags have no forward effect.

If the proposed harmful coupling matters, stop/stop improves over live/live on full validation AUC; recovery to incumbent is a separate stronger condition. AUC improvement below incumbent is only partial recovery.

Gate-only and value-only effects identify which explicit paths matter; the interaction contrast is AUC(stop,stop)-AUC(stop,live)-AUC(live,stop)+AUC(live,live). Directional predictions for individual paths are left open because uniform r0040 pools also failed.

Under independent inputs and fixed gates, value-path Jacobian is g_i/(1+M) times identity; the gate-score Jacobian is g_i(1-g_i)(v_i-y)/(1+M). Stopped paths have zero derivative to those operands, while classifier derivatives persist.

Host full-population AUC/logloss/cost are decisive. Existing hour/history/action/frequency/missing-field slices, with counts, remain exploratory; a model-supplied first512 diagnostic is not a population estimate.
falsifiers: A fixed-state forward or initialization mismatch invalidates isolation and must be corrected before causal interpretation.
If no stopped cell improves over live/live, harmful extra-path coupling is unsupported in this implementation and budget. This does not refute semantic pools generally.
If stopped cells improve over live/live but all remain below incumbent, do not select them as best model or claim the original representation problem is solved.
A candidate gain that reverses in paired seeds43/44 is preliminary/unrepeated; a gate-only and value-only reversal rejects a simple additive path explanation.
Even repeated controlled benefit supports a backward-path intervention, not an actual negative gradient dot-product, calibration claim, external method transfer or novelty claim.
alternative_explanations: Added classifier capacity or feature noise may cause the deficit; stopping representation gradients leaves both present.
Shared scorer saturation may be an effect of training rather than a cause.
Stop-gradient changes conditioning and implicit regularization and may help without a destructive direction-of-gradient conflict.
Representation drift under the parent path, label sparsity, hash collisions, limited three-epoch training or temporal distribution shift may dominate.
Single-seed variation, checkpoint selection and repeated validation search can explain small differences; no held-out test is available.
